name: Kakatiya Kingdom
hint: A major Telugu-speaking power known for Warangal Fort, irrigation works, and the reign of Rudrama Devi.
region: Deccan; mainly present-day Telangana and parts of Andhra Pradesh
ruler: Rudrama Devi; Prataparudra II

name: Eastern Chalukya Kingdom
hint: A long-lasting Vengi-based kingdom connected through conflict and marriage alliances with the Cholas.
region: Eastern Deccan; coastal Andhra Pradesh
ruler: Kubja Vishnuvardhana; Rajaraja Narendra
modern_city: Vengi region; later Rajamahendravaram area, Andhra Pradesh

name: Kingdom of Mysore
hint: A South Indian kingdom associated with the Wadiyars and, in the 18th century, Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan.
region: Southern Deccan; present-day Karnataka and neighbouring areas at different times
ruler: Wadiyar rulers; Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan during the late 18th century
modern_city: Mysore; Srirangapatna was an important capital under Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan

name: Maratha Kingdom under Shivaji Maharaj
hint: A kingdom founded by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, known for forts, regional administration, and mobile warfare.
region: Western Deccan; centred on present-day Maharashtra
ruler: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj; Sambhaji; Rajaram
modern_city: Raigad and other forts in Maharashtra

name: Hoysala Kingdom
hint: Known for intricately carved temples at Belur and Halebidu and a powerful medieval presence in southern India.
region: Southern Deccan; mainly present-day Karnataka
ruler: Vishnuvardhana; Ballala II; Ballala III

name: Ahom Kingdom
hint: A long-lasting northeastern kingdom remembered for resisting Mughal expansion, including the Battle of Saraighat.
region: Brahmaputra Valley; present-day Assam
ruler: Sukaphaa; Suhungmung; Pratap Singha; associated commander Lachit Borphukan
modern_city: Charaideo, Garhgaon and Rangpur at different periods; Assam

name: Mewar Kingdom
hint: A Rajput kingdom associated with Chittorgarh, Rana Sanga, and Maharana Pratap.
region: Southern Rajasthan
ruler: Rana Sanga; Maharana Pratap; later rulers of Udaipur

name: Chera Kingdom
hint: A major Tamil-Malayalam-region polity associated with western-coast trade and the spice routes.
region: Parts of present-day Kerala and western Tamil Nadu
ruler: Senguttuvan is celebrated in Tamil tradition; Chera rulers are known from inscriptions and literature
modern_city: Vanchi is named in literary sources; its exact identification is debated

name: Pandya Kingdom
hint: A Tamil kingdom centred on Madurai, known for temple patronage, trade, and pearl fisheries.
region: Southern Tamil Nadu
ruler: Nedunjeliyan in early Tamil tradition; Jatavarman Sundara Pandyan in the medieval period

name: Vijayanagara Empire
hint: A major South Indian imperial state associated with Hampi and Krishnadevaraya.
region: Southern India and the Deccan
ruler: Harihara I; Bukka I; Krishnadevaraya

name: Kingdom of Travancore
hint: A southern Kerala kingdom known for state-building, temple traditions, and a long royal history.
region: Southern Kerala and nearby areas
ruler: Marthanda Varma; Swathi Thirunal; Chithira Thirunal

name: Yadava Kingdom of Dwarka (traditional)
hint: In Hindu epic tradition, Krishna and the Yadavas are associated with Dwarka after leaving Mathura.
region: Traditional setting on the Gujarat coast
ruler: Krishna and the Yadavas in the Mahabharata/Puranic tradition

name: Kingdom / State of Jhansi
hint: Widely remembered through Rani Lakshmibai and the Indian Rebellion of 1857.
region: Bundelkhand; present-day Uttar Pradesh
ruler: Gangadhar Rao; Rani Lakshmibai

name: Kamarupa Kingdom
hint: An important early kingdom in Assam, known through inscriptions and rulers such as Bhaskaravarman.
region: Northeastern India; centred in the Brahmaputra Valley
ruler: Bhaskaravarman; rulers of the Varman and later dynasties
modern_city: Pragjyotishpura, often associated with the Guwahati region; Assam

name: Kuninda Kingdom
hint: A Himalayan-region polity known largely from coins and archaeological evidence.
region: Himalayan foothills; parts of present-day Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh
ruler: Specific rulers are not securely established; coins are key evidence

name: Kingdom of Cochin
hint: A Kerala kingdom involved in Indian Ocean commerce and later Portuguese, Dutch, and British-era politics.
region: Central Kerala
ruler: Sakthan Thampuran is a notable later ruler

name: Patiala State
hint: A prominent Sikh princely state in the Punjab region.
region: Eastern Punjab; present-day Punjab, India
ruler: Ala Singh; Maharaja Bhupinder Singh

name: Kashmir Kingdom (medieval)
hint: A Himalayan kingdom known for Sanskrit scholarship, art, and rulers such as Lalitaditya in the Karkota period.
region: Kashmir Valley and adjoining Himalayan areas at different times
ruler: Lalitaditya Muktapida (Karkota period); other dynasties ruled in later centuries
modern_city: Kashmir Valley; Srinagar and other centres

name: Marwar Kingdom
hint: A Rajput kingdom centred on Jodhpur, with major forts and desert trade routes.
region: Western Rajasthan
ruler: Rao Jodha; Jaswant Singh; Ajit Singh

name: Bharatpur State
hint: A Jat-ruled state known for its fortifications and the rule of Maharaja Suraj Mal.
region: Eastern Rajasthan and nearby north Indian areas
ruler: Maharaja Suraj Mal; Jawahar Singh

name: Chola Kingdom
hint: A Tamil power associated with Rajaraja I, Rajendra I, monumental temples, and overseas connections.
region: Tamil Nadu and, at its height, parts of Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia-facing maritime networks
ruler: Rajaraja Chola I; Rajendra Chola I
modern_city: Thanjavur and Gangaikonda Cholapuram, Tamil Nadu

name: Jaffna Kingdom
hint: A Tamil kingdom in northern Sri Lanka with maritime links and a capital at Nallur.
region: Northern Sri Lanka
ruler: Aryacakravarti rulers

name: Gajapati Kingdom of Odisha
hint: A powerful Odishan state associated with Kapilendra Deva and the Jagannath tradition.
region: Odisha and neighbouring parts of eastern/southern India at its height
ruler: Kapilendra Deva; Purushottama Deva; Prataparudra Deva

name: Madurai Nayak Kingdom
hint: A Tamil kingdom known for temple-building, palace architecture, and the rule of Tirumala Nayak.
region: Southern Tamil Nadu
ruler: Viswanatha Nayak; Tirumala Nayak; Rani Mangammal

name: Amber Kingdom
hint: A Kachwaha Rajput kingdom associated with Amber Fort and rulers who participated in Mughal-era politics.
region: Eastern Rajasthan
ruler: Raja Man Singh I; Mirza Raja Jai Singh I

name: Jaisalmer Kingdom
hint: A desert kingdom whose fortified capital sat on important caravan routes.
region: Western Rajasthan / Thar Desert
ruler: Rawal Jaisal; later Bhati rulers

name: Kangra Kingdom
hint: A Himalayan kingdom associated with the Katoch dynasty and the historic Kangra Fort.
region: Himachal Pradesh and surrounding Himalayan foothills
ruler: Katoch rulers; Maharaja Sansar Chand is a notable later ruler
modern_city: Kangra Fort / Kangra Valley, Himachal Pradesh

name: Chitradurga Nayaka Kingdom
hint: A fortified inland state remembered for Chitradurga Fort and its Nayaka rulers.
region: Central Karnataka
ruler: Madakari Nayaka is a prominent later ruler

name: Haryanka Dynasty of Magadha
hint: The early Magadhan dynasty of Bimbisara and Ajatashatru that began Magadha's rise as the leading power of the Gangetic plain.
region: Middle Gangetic plain; present-day Bihar and neighbouring areas
ruler: Bimbisara; Ajatashatru; Udayin

name: Nanda Dynasty
hint: A Magadhan dynasty remembered for its vast army and treasury, overthrown by Chandragupta Maurya with Chanakya's help.
region: Gangetic plain and parts of central and eastern India
ruler: Mahapadma Nanda; Dhana Nanda

name: Maurya Empire
hint: India's first great pan-subcontinental empire, associated with Chandragupta, Chanakya's statecraft and the edicts of Ashoka.
region: Most of the Indian subcontinent and parts of present-day Afghanistan
ruler: Chandragupta Maurya; Bindusara; Ashoka

name: Shunga Dynasty
hint: The Magadhan successors of the Mauryas, associated with Pushyamitra Shunga and the growth of Sanchi and Bharhut art.
region: Central and northern India
ruler: Pushyamitra Shunga; Agnimitra

name: Kingdom of Kalinga (Kharavela's Era)
hint: An eastern coastal power known for the Kalinga War against Ashoka and for Kharavela's Hathigumpha inscription.
region: Odisha and neighbouring coastal regions
ruler: Kharavela (Mahameghavahana line)
modern_city: Sisupalgarh and Udayagiri–Khandagiri, near Bhubaneswar, Odisha

name: Satavahana Dynasty
hint: A Deccan dynasty that controlled Roman-era trade routes and patronised Buddhist art at Amaravati and the Western Ghats caves.
region: Deccan; present-day Maharashtra, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh
ruler: Simuka; Gautamiputra Satakarni; Vasishthiputra Pulumavi
modern_city: Pratishthana (Paithan), Maharashtra; Amaravati / Dharanikota, Andhra Pradesh

name: Kushan Empire
hint: A Central Asian-origin empire on the Silk Road, famous for Kanishka, Gandhara and Mathura art, and the spread of Buddhism.
region: Northwestern South Asia, Afghanistan and Central Asia
ruler: Kujula Kadphises; Vima Kadphises; Kanishka I

name: Western Satraps (Western Kshatrapas)
hint: A Saka dynasty that ruled Gujarat and Malwa, known for Rudradaman I's Junagadh inscription and its Indian Ocean trade.
region: Western India; present-day Gujarat, Malwa and Saurashtra
ruler: Nahapana; Rudradaman I

name: Vakataka Dynasty
hint: A central Indian dynasty allied by marriage to the Guptas and remembered as patrons of the Ajanta cave paintings.
region: Deccan and central India; present-day Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh
ruler: Pravarasena I; Rudrasena II; Harishena

name: Pallava Dynasty
hint: A Tamil-region dynasty known for rock-cut and structural temples at Mamallapuram and for its rivalry with the Chalukyas.
region: Northern Tamil Nadu and southern Andhra Pradesh
ruler: Mahendravarman I; Narasimhavarman I; Nandivarman II

name: Gupta Empire
hint: Often called India's classical age, associated with Samudragupta, Chandragupta II and advances in science, literature and art.
region: Northern and central India
ruler: Chandragupta I; Samudragupta; Chandragupta II; Skandagupta
modern_city: Pataliputra, Bihar; Prayagraj and Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh

name: Kadamba Dynasty of Banavasi
hint: The first major Kannada-region dynasty to use the Kannada language in administration, founded by Mayurasharma.
region: Northwestern Karnataka and the Konkan coast
ruler: Mayurasharma; Kakusthavarma

name: Western Ganga Dynasty
hint: A long-lived Karnataka dynasty associated with Talakadu and the Jain colossus at Shravanabelagola.
region: Southern Karnataka
ruler: Kongunivarma Madhava; Durvinita; Rachamalla IV; minister Chavundaraya

name: Chalukyas of Badami
hint: A Deccan imperial power under Pulakeshin II, who checked Harsha, and a builder of the temples at Aihole and Pattadakal.
region: Deccan; present-day Karnataka and Maharashtra, at times beyond
ruler: Pulakeshin I; Pulakeshin II; Vikramaditya II

name: Pushyabhuti (Vardhana) Dynasty
hint: The north Indian dynasty of Harsha, whose court was described by the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang.
region: Northern India; Thanesar and the Kannauj region
ruler: Prabhakaravardhana; Harshavardhana

name: Gurjara-Pratihara Dynasty
hint: A north Indian power that held Kannauj, resisted Arab expansion from Sindh, and fought in the tripartite struggle.
region: Northern and western India; Rajasthan, Malwa and the Gangetic plain
ruler: Nagabhata I; Mihira Bhoja; Mahendrapala I

name: Pala Empire
hint: A Buddhist-patron dynasty of Bengal and Bihar that sustained Nalanda, Vikramashila and Odantapuri.
region: Eastern India; present-day Bengal, Bihar and Bangladesh
ruler: Gopala; Dharmapala; Devapala; Ramapala

name: Rashtrakuta Dynasty
hint: A Deccan imperial dynasty that contested Kannauj and built the Kailasa temple at Ellora.
region: Deccan; present-day Karnataka and Maharashtra, with reach into north and south India
ruler: Dantidurga; Krishna I; Amoghavarsha I; Krishna III

name: Paramara Dynasty of Malwa
hint: A Malwa dynasty best known for the scholar-king Bhoja, patron of learning and builder of Dhar and Bhojpur.
region: Malwa; present-day western Madhya Pradesh and nearby areas
ruler: Siyaka; Munja; Bhoja

name: Hindu Shahi Dynasty
hint: A dynasty of the Kabul valley and Punjab that resisted the Ghaznavids under Jayapala and Anandapala.
region: Eastern Afghanistan, northwestern Punjab and the Indus region
ruler: Lalliya; Jayapala; Anandapala; Trilochanapala

name: Chandela Dynasty
hint: A Bundelkhand dynasty remembered for the Khajuraho temples and the forts of Kalinjar and Mahoba.
region: Bundelkhand; present-day Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
ruler: Dhanga; Vidyadhara; Paramardi

name: Chaulukya (Solanki) Dynasty of Gujarat
hint: A wealthy Gujarat dynasty linked with the Modhera Sun Temple, Rani ki Vav and Jain patronage under Kumarapala.
region: Gujarat and parts of Rajasthan and Malwa
ruler: Mularaja; Bhima I; Jayasimha Siddharaja; Kumarapala

name: Western Chalukya Dynasty (Kalyani)
hint: A Deccan dynasty that rivalled the Cholas and patronised Kannada and Sanskrit scholarship under Vikramaditya VI.
region: Deccan; present-day Karnataka and Maharashtra
ruler: Tailapa II; Someshvara I; Vikramaditya VI

name: Chahamana (Chauhan) Dynasty of Shakambhari
hint: A Rajput dynasty of Ajmer and Delhi, associated with Prithviraj III and the Battles of Tarain.
region: Eastern Rajasthan and the Delhi region
ruler: Vigraharaja IV; Prithviraj III

name: Sena Dynasty of Bengal
hint: A Bengal dynasty of the 11th–12th centuries, linked with Lakshmanasena and the poet Jayadeva.
region: Bengal; present-day West Bengal and Bangladesh
ruler: Vijayasena; Ballala Sena; Lakshmanasena

name: Yadava (Seuna) Dynasty of Devagiri
hint: The historically documented Yadava kingdom of the western Deccan, famous for Devagiri fort and its wealth.
region: Western Deccan; present-day Maharashtra
ruler: Bhillama V; Singhana II; Ramachandra

name: Delhi Sultanate
hint: The north Indian sultanate ruled by five successive dynasties, from the Mamluks to the Lodis.
region: Northern India, at times reaching the Deccan and the south
ruler: Iltutmish; Alauddin Khalji; Muhammad bin Tughluq; Ibrahim Lodi

name: Kingdom of Calicut (Zamorin Dynasty)
hint: A Malabar coast kingdom whose port of Calicut was a hub of the spice trade and where Vasco da Gama landed in 1498.
region: Northern Kerala (Malabar)
ruler: Zamorin (Samoothiri) rulers; naval commanders such as the Kunjali Marakkars

name: Bahmani Sultanate
hint: The first independent Muslim kingdom of the Deccan, whose breakup produced the five Deccan sultanates.
region: Deccan; present-day Karnataka, Maharashtra and Telangana
ruler: Alauddin Bahman Shah; Muhammad Shah I; minister Mahmud Gawan

name: Bengal Sultanate
hint: A wealthy independent sultanate of Bengal known for its trade, mosque architecture and diplomatic ties with Ming China.
region: Bengal; present-day West Bengal and Bangladesh
ruler: Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah; Ghiyasuddin Azam Shah; Alauddin Hussain Shah

name: Manikya Dynasty of Tripura
hint: A northeastern dynasty documented in the Rajmala chronicle, ruling Tripura into the 20th century.
region: Northeastern India; present-day Tripura and parts of Bangladesh
ruler: Dhanya Manikya; Govinda Manikya; Birchandra Manikya

name: Adil Shahi Sultanate of Bijapur
hint: A Deccan sultanate famous for the Gol Gumbaz and a refined Deccani court culture.
region: Western Deccan; present-day Karnataka and Maharashtra
ruler: Yusuf Adil Shah; Ibrahim Adil Shah II; Muhammad Adil Shah

name: Qutb Shahi Dynasty of Golconda
hint: The Telugu-Deccan sultanate that founded Hyderabad and controlled the famed Golconda diamond trade.
region: Eastern Deccan; present-day Telangana and coastal Andhra Pradesh
ruler: Quli Qutb Mulk; Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah; Abul Hasan Tana Shah

name: Mughal Empire
hint: The great Indo-Islamic empire of Babur, Akbar, Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb, one of the richest states of its age.
region: Most of the Indian subcontinent at its height
ruler: Babur; Akbar; Shah Jahan; Aurangzeb

name: Sur Empire
hint: A short-lived Afghan-origin empire of Sher Shah Suri, remembered for the Grand Trunk Road and administrative reform.
region: Northern India
ruler: Sher Shah Suri; Islam Shah

name: Hyderabad State (Asaf Jahi Nizams)
hint: The largest and among the wealthiest princely states of British India, ruled by the Nizams.
region: Deccan; Telangana and parts of Karnataka and Maharashtra
ruler: Asaf Jah I (Nizam-ul-Mulk); Mir Osman Ali Khan

name: Sikh Empire
hint: A Punjab-based empire under Maharaja Ranjit Singh with a modernised Khalsa army, annexed by the British in 1849.
region: Punjab, Kashmir and the northwestern frontier
ruler: Ranjit Singh; Hari Singh Nalwa

name: Indo-Greek Kingdom
hint: A Hellenistic kingdom in northwestern South Asia known for Greek-Indian cultural exchange and coinage.
region: Parts of present-day Afghanistan and Pakistan, with varying reach into northwestern India
ruler: Menander I (Milinda) is among its best-known rulers
modern_city: Sagala (often identified with Sialkot) and other centres; identifications vary

name: Kingdom of Macedon
hint: The Greek kingdom that Alexander the Great ruled before and during his conquests.
region: Northern Greece and surrounding Balkan regions
ruler: Philip II; Alexander the Great

name: Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt
hint: A Hellenistic Egyptian kingdom founded by Ptolemy I and ended after Cleopatra VII's reign.
region: Egypt, with control of different eastern Mediterranean territories at various times
ruler: Ptolemy I Soter; Cleopatra VII

name: Seleucid State / Seleucid Empire
hint: A successor state to Alexander's empire that controlled extensive lands across western and central Asia.
region: At different times, Syria, Mesopotamia, Iran, and parts of Anatolia and Central Asia
ruler: Seleucus I Nicator; Antiochus III
modern_city: Antioch and Seleucia on the Tigris were major capitals

name: Nabataean Kingdom
hint: A desert trading kingdom known for Petra, rock-cut architecture, and control of caravan routes.
region: Modern Jordan and adjacent parts of the Arabian Peninsula and Levant
ruler: Aretas IV is a well-known ruler

name: Kingdom of Pergamon
hint: A Hellenistic kingdom known for its royal library, sculpture, and the Attalid dynasty.
region: Western Anatolia, in present-day Turkey
ruler: Attalus I; Eumenes II

name: Kingdom of Epirus
hint: A northwestern Greek kingdom associated with King Pyrrhus and his campaigns against Rome.
region: Epirus in present-day northwestern Greece and southern Albania
ruler: Pyrrhus of Epirus
modern_city: Dodona and Ambracia were important centres at different times

name: Kingdom of Armenia
hint: A kingdom positioned between Roman and Parthian powers, reaching a high point under Tigranes II.
region: Armenian Highlands; modern Armenia and surrounding regions at different times
ruler: Artaxias I; Tigranes II the Great
modern_city: Artaxata and Tigranocerta were important capitals

name: Kingdom of Pontus
hint: A Black Sea kingdom known for Mithridates VI and its long wars against Rome.
region: Northern Anatolia along the Black Sea, in present-day Turkey
ruler: Mithridates VI Eupator
modern_city: Amaseia and Sinope were important centres

name: Ryukyu Kingdom
hint: An island kingdom known for maritime trade and diplomatic links with China, Japan, and Southeast Asia.
region: Ryukyu Islands, centred on Okinawa
ruler: Shō dynasty; Shō Shin and Shō Tai are notable rulers

name: Kingdom of England
hint: A European kingdom associated with medieval monarchs, the Tudor period, and the development of parliamentary government.
region: England and, at different times, territories under English crown control
ruler: Athelstan; Henry VIII; Elizabeth I
modern_city: London became the principal royal and political centre

name: Kingdom of Scotland
hint: A northern British kingdom associated with the Wars of Scottish Independence and Robert the Bruce.
region: Scotland, in the northern part of Great Britain
ruler: Kenneth MacAlpin (traditional early association); Robert the Bruce; Mary, Queen of Scots
modern_city: Scone and Edinburgh were important royal centres

name: Kingdom of Wessex
hint: An Anglo-Saxon kingdom associated with Alfred the Great and the resistance to Viking incursions.
region: Southern England
ruler: Egbert; Alfred the Great; Edward the Elder
modern_city: Winchester and other royal centres in southern England

name: Tikal Maya Kingdom / City-State
hint: A major Maya city-state known for monumental temples, inscriptions, and rulers such as Jasaw Chan K'awiil I.
region: Petén region of present-day Guatemala
ruler: Jasaw Chan K'awiil I; numerous other rulers known from inscriptions

name: Cusco Polity / Early Inca State
hint: The early Cusco polity developed into the Inca Empire, which built a vast Andean road and administrative network.
region: Andes of present-day Peru, later extending across parts of western South America
ruler: Manco Cápac is traditional; Pachacuti is central to imperial expansion

name: Kingdom of Babylon (Old and Neo-Babylonian)
hint: A Mesopotamian kingdom associated with Hammurabi's law code and Nebuchadnezzar II's rebuilding of Babylon.
region: Mesopotamia; present-day Iraq
ruler: Hammurabi; Nebuchadnezzar II

name: New Kingdom of Egypt
hint: Egypt's imperial age, from Ahmose I to Ramesses II, marked by conquests and monuments at Thebes.
region: Egypt, with control reaching Nubia and the Levant
ruler: Ahmose I; Hatshepsut; Thutmose III; Ramesses II

name: Kingdom of Kush (Napata and Meroë)
hint: A Nubian kingdom that ruled Egypt as the 25th Dynasty and later flourished at Meroë as an iron-working centre.
region: Nile valley south of Egypt; present-day Sudan
ruler: Piye; Taharqa; Amanirenas

name: Achaemenid Empire
hint: The first Persian world empire, built by Cyrus the Great and organised under Darius I through satrapies and the Royal Road.
region: Iran, Mesopotamia, Anatolia, Egypt and Central Asia
ruler: Cyrus II; Darius I; Xerxes I

name: Han Dynasty
hint: A foundational Chinese dynasty that expanded the empire, opened the Silk Road and shaped Confucian state ideology.
region: China, with reach into Central Asia and Korea
ruler: Gaozu; Emperor Wu; Guangwu

name: Roman Empire (Principate and Western Empire)
hint: The Mediterranean empire of Augustus and Trajan, famed for its legions, law and engineering.
region: Mediterranean basin, Western Europe and the Near East
ruler: Augustus; Trajan; Constantine I

name: Kingdom of Aksum
hint: An East African trading kingdom that adopted Christianity under Ezana and minted its own coinage.
region: Northern Ethiopia and Eritrea, with Red Sea influence
ruler: Ezana; Kaleb

name: Sasanian Empire
hint: The last pre-Islamic Persian empire, a rival of Rome and Byzantium under Shapur I and Khosrow I.
region: Iran, Mesopotamia and the Caucasus, with Central Asian reach
ruler: Ardashir I; Shapur I; Khosrow I

name: Byzantine Empire (Eastern Roman Empire)
hint: The long-lived eastern continuation of Rome, centred on Constantinople and known for Justinian and the Hagia Sophia.
region: Eastern Mediterranean, Anatolia and the Balkans
ruler: Justinian I; Heraclius; Basil II

name: Frankish Kingdom and Carolingian Empire
hint: The Merovingian and Carolingian realm of Clovis and Charlemagne that shaped early medieval western Europe.
region: Present-day France, Germany, Belgium and northern Italy
ruler: Clovis I; Charles Martel; Charlemagne

name: Tang Dynasty
hint: A golden age of Chinese poetry, trade and cosmopolitan culture centred on the capital Chang'an.
region: China, with influence across Central and East Asia
ruler: Taizong; Wu Zetian; Xuanzong

name: Abbasid Caliphate
hint: The Baghdad-based caliphate of Harun al-Rashid and al-Ma'mun, a centre of science and translation.
region: Middle East, North Africa and Central Asia at its height
ruler: Al-Mansur; Harun al-Rashid; Al-Ma'mun

name: Khmer Empire
hint: The Southeast Asian empire of Angkor, builder of Angkor Wat and the Bayon.
region: Cambodia, with reach into Thailand, Laos and southern Vietnam
ruler: Jayavarman II; Suryavarman II; Jayavarman VII

name: Kingdom of France (Capetian to Bourbon)
hint: A major European monarchy from Hugh Capet to Louis XIV, marked by centralised royal power and court culture.
region: Present-day France and overseas holdings
ruler: Philip II Augustus; Louis IX; Louis XIV

name: Mongol Empire
hint: The largest contiguous land empire in history, founded by Genghis Khan with mobile cavalry armies.
region: Eurasia from China to Eastern Europe
ruler: Genghis Khan; Ögedei; Möngke; Kublai Khan

name: Mali Empire
hint: A West African empire of gold and salt trade, famed for Mansa Musa and the scholarship of Timbuktu.
region: West Africa; present-day Mali, Senegal, Guinea and neighbours
ruler: Sundiata Keita; Mansa Musa
modern_city: Niani and Timbuktu region, West Africa

name: Ottoman Empire
hint: A multi-continental empire that took Constantinople in 1453 and peaked under Suleiman the Magnificent.
region: Anatolia, the Balkans, the Middle East and North Africa
ruler: Osman I; Mehmed II; Suleiman I

name: Ming Dynasty
hint: The Chinese dynasty of the Yongle Emperor and Zheng He's voyages, which rebuilt the Great Wall and the Forbidden City.
region: China
ruler: Hongwu; Yongle; Wanli

name: Joseon Dynasty
hint: A long-lived Korean dynasty known for Confucian governance, the Hangul script under Sejong and Admiral Yi Sun-sin.
region: Korean Peninsula
ruler: Taejo; Sejong the Great; Yi Sun-sin (admiral)

name: Aztec Empire (Triple Alliance)
hint: The Mexica-led alliance of Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan that dominated central Mexico until 1521.
region: Central Mexico
ruler: Itzcoatl; Moctezuma I; Ahuitzotl; Moctezuma II
